findings.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131 — Sending any non-empty totpCode skips the password check (line 121), and the new backupCode branch then skips TOTP validation, so email plus one backup code logs in with no password or TOTP.

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:144 — Consuming a backup code is a non-atomic read-modify-write with no version or where-guard, so concurrent logins can reuse the same single-use code, and a lost update can bring back consumed codes or overwrite codes regenerated in the meantime.

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131 — Sending any non-empty totpCode skips the password check (line 121), and the new backupCode branch then skips TOTP validation, so email plus one backup code logs in with no password or TOTP.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds a new branch in `authorize` for `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode`, which intentionally skips TOTP validation when a backup code is provided. The finding’s core claim—that supplying any non-empty `totpCode` bypasses the password check (and thus allows login with email+backupCode without a password)—is not shown or modified in this diff; the password-verification logic around the referenced “line 121” is not present here, and nothing in the added backup-code branch indicates it disables or bypasses whatever password check already exists earlier in the function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:144 — Consuming a backup code is a non-atomic read-modify-write with no version or where-guard, so concurrent logins can reuse the same single-use code, and a lost update can bring back consumed codes or overwrite codes regenerated in the meantime.

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:144 — backupCode is not type-checked, so a JSON body sending it as an array, object, or number throws a TypeError whose raw message is passed through to the client as res.error.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the new backup-code path assumes `credentials.backupCode` is a string and calls `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. If a client submits a non-string (e.g., array/object/number) this will throw a runtime `TypeError` (since `replaceAll` won’t exist), which is not caught in the shown code path and would result in a failed auth request (and potentially an unexpected error string returned). The diff introduces this unvalidated string method call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61 — A non-string req.body.backupCode (array, object, or number) crashes replaceAll with an unhandled 500, and the missing-key path at line 51 also throws instead of returning a JSON error.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` without validating that `req.body.backupCode` is a string. If a client sends a non-string JSON value (array/object/number), this will throw a `TypeError` and result in a 500 rather than a controlled 4xx response. Also, the missing encryption key path does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` instead of returning a JSON error response in this branch (no response shown here), which can likewise surface as a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:137 — Once every code is used the array holds only nulls, so users get "incorrect" instead of MissingBackupCodes; there is also no way to regenerate codes (setup is blocked while 2FA is enabled), so users who enabled 2FA before this change, or who missed the post-enable screen, can never get codes.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup codes are stored as an encrypted JSON array and consumed by setting `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypting. When all codes are used, `user.backupCodes` is still a non-null string, so `if (!user.backupCodes) throw MissingBackupCodes` will not trigger, and `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` will return `-1`, causing `IncorrectBackupCode` instead of a more accurate "no backup codes remaining"/MissingBackupCodes condition. This incorrect error behavior is directly implied by the diff. The claim about there being no regeneration path is not directly verifiable from this diff, but the exhausted-codes handling issue is.

apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:53 — The assertion expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy() checks a Promise and always passes; the FIXME admits this, and it now hides that this test never clicks backup-codes-close, so the switch is never actually checked.

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts the line `await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` passes a Promise (from `isChecked()`) directly into `expect(...)`. As written, `toBeTruthy()` will evaluate the Promise object (truthy) rather than the resolved boolean, so the assertion can pass even when the switch is not checked—consistent with the adjacent `FIXME` comment added in the diff. However, the finding’s claim that the test “never clicks backup-codes-close” is not supported by the diff: the test explicitly clicks `page.getByTestId("backup-codes-close")` later.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 — No test covers logging in with a backup code, disabling 2FA with one, single-use enforcement, or rejecting a wrong code, so the security-critical server paths are untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new security-relevant backup-code flows on both client and server (e.g., login via `credentials.backupCode` in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` with single-use deletion, and disabling 2FA via `req.body.backupCode` in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`). The Playwright test file `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` explicitly notes missing coverage (`// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup code tests`) and the added assertions only cover backup-code display/copy/download UI after enabling 2FA, not logging in with a backup code, disabling 2FA with one, wrong-code rejection, or single-use enforcement. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:166 — At the DisplayBackupCodes step 2FA is already enabled server-side, but closing the dialog via Esc/overlay (onOpenChange) skips onEnable and resetState, so the parent still shows 2FA as disabled and reopening the dialog lands on the stale backup-codes step.

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, after a successful enable (`handleEnable`), the code sets `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` and does *not* call `onEnable()` yet (it’s only called by the explicit “close” button in the DisplayBackupCodes footer). The Dialog is controlled by `open`/`onOpenChange`, but `onOpenChange` is passed through directly (`<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>`) with no wrapper to call `resetState()` or `onEnable()` when the user dismisses the dialog via Esc/overlay. Since the modal’s internal React state persists when `open` toggles, reopening can land on the stale `DisplayBackupCodes` step, and the parent won’t be notified via `onEnable()` even though the server-side enable already happened.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61 — req.body.backupCode is not type-checked, so a truthy non-string (number or array) makes replaceAll throw an unhandled 500 instead of returning IncorrectBackupCode.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch is entered on any truthy `req.body.backupCode` (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)`). Inside, it unconditionally calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. If a client sends a non-string truthy value (e.g., number, object, array), `replaceAll` is undefined and this will throw, resulting in an unhandled 500 rather than returning `IncorrectBackupCode`/a 4xx. The diff shows no type guard/coercion before calling `replaceAll`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:137 — Once all codes are used the stored array is all nulls but still non-null, so users get IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes and are never told their codes are exhausted.

adjudication.rationale: In `next-auth-options.ts`, backup codes are stored as an encrypted JSON array. When a backup code is used, the code sets `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypts the array, but it never checks whether all entries are now `null` (i.e., exhausted). The only `MissingBackupCodes` check is `if (!user.backupCodes)`, which won’t trigger once the encrypted string exists. After exhaustion, any entered code won’t be found (`indexOf(...) === -1`) and the user will always get `IncorrectBackupCode` rather than an error indicating no backup codes remain.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql:2 — Existing 2FA-enabled users get NULL backupCodes with no backfill, and setup.ts:42 rejects them (TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled), so they can only get codes by disabling and re-enabling 2FA; backup login just returns MissingBackupCodes

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:148 — Consuming a backup code is a non-atomic read-decrypt-modify-write with no version check, so concurrent logins can reuse the same single-use code (lost update on backupCodes)

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:148 — Used codes are stored as nulls instead of being removed, so a fully used set stays non-null and the MissingBackupCodes branch (line 137) never fires; users get IncorrectBackupCode instead

But when a code is used, the diff sets `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypts/stores the array back into `user.backupCodes`, so the field remains non-null even when all codes have been consumed. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:149 — Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-decrypt-modify-write with no transaction/optimistic check, so concurrent logins can reuse the same single-use code or a later write can resurrect an already-consumed code (lost update).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup code consumption does a read/decrypt -> modify in memory (`backupCodes[index] = null`) -> write back with `prisma.user.update(...)` without any transaction, row lock, or optimistic concurrency check. Two concurrent logins can both decrypt the same original `backupCodes` array and then write back different modified versions, causing a lost update (e.g., consuming code A and code B concurrently can result in the later write reintroducing the other still-unused code). This breaks the intended single-use property and can allow reuse/resurrection under concurrency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139 — JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) is unguarded; a corrupt ciphertext or rotated CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY throws a raw SyntaxError/crypto error instead of a mapped ErrorCode, surfacing as an opaque login failure with no logging context.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds backup-code login in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` where it does `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY))` with no try/catch. If `user.backupCodes` is corrupted or decrypt fails due to a key mismatch/rotation, `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and/or `JSON.parse(...)` can throw and will not be converted to an `ErrorCode` (only the missing-key case is logged/mapped), causing an unexpected/opaque login failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:58 — Unguarded JSON.parse/symmetricDecrypt of stored backup codes throws inside the API handler, producing an unstructured 500 rather than a JSON error response.

If `user.backupCodes` is corrupted or decryption fails, either `symmetricDecrypt` or `JSON.parse` will throw. The diff shows no handling around that call in this branch (it only checks for missing env key / missing field), so this can crash the handler path rather than returning a controlled JSON error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:51 — Missing-encryption-key case throws inside the Next API handler (500 with no JSON body) instead of returning res.status(500).json({ error: InternalServerError }) like setup.ts does.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61 — req.body.backupCode.replaceAll is called without a string type check, so a non-string backupCode in the JSON body throws a TypeError and yields a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:278 — navigator.clipboard.writeText promise is neither awaited nor caught, so the success toast is shown even when the write rejects (permission denied), and navigator.clipboard is undefined in non-secure (http self-hosted) contexts causing a thrown TypeError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:68 — Setup overwrites stored backupCodes and secret before enable succeeds, so concurrent setup calls (e.g. two tabs) can cause the modal to display backup codes that no longer match what is persisted when enable later succeeds.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, each setup call generates a new `secret` and `backupCodes` and immediately persists them via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...), twoFactorSecret: symmetricEncrypt(secret, ...), twoFactorEnabled: false }})`, then returns the generated `backupCodes` to the client. Because this state is written before the user completes the enable step, a second concurrent setup call (e.g., another tab) will overwrite the stored `backupCodes`/`twoFactorSecret` while the first tab is still showing the previously returned codes, creating a real race/inconsistency between what the modal displays and what is persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:137 — When all codes are consumed (array of nulls) users get IncorrectBackupCode rather than MissingBackupCodes, and pre-existing 2FA users have null backupCodes with no regeneration path other than disable/re-enable.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code login checks `if (!user.backupCodes) throw MissingBackupCodes`, but once codes are consumed it persists the encrypted array with entries set to `null` (`backupCodes[index] = null` + re-encrypt). In that state `user.backupCodes` is still non-null, so a later attempt will fall through to `indexOf(...) === -1` and throw `IncorrectBackupCode`, not `MissingBackupCodes`. That’s a real edge-case behavior implied by the diff, but it’s not clearly a correctness defect since `MissingBackupCodes` is only used when the DB field is absent. Separately, the diff only generates/stores backup codes during TOTP setup (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`) and displays them only in the enable flow; there’s no regeneration path shown for users who already had 2FA enabled with `backupCodes` null, so the new “Lost access” UI may be less useful for that cohort. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131 — Backup-code branch takes precedence over TOTP while password check (line 121) is skipped whenever any totpCode is sent, so email + junk totpCode + one backup code logs in with no password and no TOTP.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:144 — Backup-code consume is a non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt, indexOf, re-encrypt, update), so concurrent login requests can replay the same single-use code.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the backup-code path performs a read-modify-write sequence: decrypt `user.backupCodes`, `indexOf` the provided code, then set `backupCodes[index] = null` and persist via `prisma.user.update(...)` with re-encrypted JSON. This update is not guarded by a transaction/locking or a conditional update that ensures the code was still unused at write time, so two concurrent login requests using the same backup code could both pass validation before either update commits, effectively allowing replay of a single-use code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61 — req.body.backupCode is not type-checked; a non-string JSON value (number/array/object) makes replaceAll throw an unhandled 500.

If a client sends a truthy non-string JSON value (e.g., `{}`/`[]`/number), `replaceAll` will be undefined and throw, resulting in an unhandled 500 in this handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:144 — Backup codes are compared with Array.indexOf (non-constant-time) instead of a timing-safe comparison.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup code verification uses `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` to locate a matching secret. This performs variable-time comparisons/iteration (early exit when a match is found) rather than a timing-safe equality check, which is a security defect for secret-token validation. The same pattern also appears in the new API handler (`disable.ts`) via `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:68 — Backup codes are stored reversibly encrypted with the shared app key instead of being hashed individually, so a DB and key compromise exposes all usable codes.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, backup codes are generated and stored as `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` (i.e., decryptable with the shared app key). The login flow (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`) and disable endpoint decrypt `user.backupCodes` to validate codes, confirming the design relies on reversible storage. This means a DB + app-key compromise exposes all still-valid backup codes, which is a concrete security weakness introduced by the diff; hashing per-code would avoid plaintext recovery while still allowing verification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:71 — resetState does not clear backupCodes state or revoke the blob URL, so plaintext codes linger in client memory after the dialog closes.

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, `resetState()` only calls `setPassword("")`, `setErrorMessage(null)`, and `setStep(SetupStep.ConfirmPassword)`, but does not clear `backupCodes`/`backupCodesUrl` nor revoke the created object URL. The blob URL is only revoked when generating a new one in `handleSetup` (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`), so closing/canceling the dialog leaves the plaintext backup codes array and an active blob URL in memory for the lifetime of the component.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131 — The new backup-code branch in credentials authorize (match, single-use nulling at line 148, IncorrectBackupCode, MissingBackupCodes) has no unit, integration, or e2e test, so a security-sensitive change to login auth ships unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new security-sensitive login logic in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` to accept `credentials.backupCode`, decrypt `user.backupCodes`, validate it, and then persist an updated encrypted list with the used code nulled out. In the shown test changes, `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` only exercises enabling 2FA and interacting with the backup-codes UI (download/copy/close), and even includes a TODO/FIXME noting missing backup-code tests. There is no unit/integration/e2e coverage in this diff that verifies backup-code login behavior (success/failure, single-use invalidation, MissingBackupCodes/IncorrectBackupCode paths), so the finding is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 — A TODO stands in for the core backup-code tests: no test logs in with a backup code, and nothing checks that a used code is rejected on the next try (single-use).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial backup-code behavior (login via `credentials.backupCode` with single-use invalidation in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, and backup-code handling in disable endpoint). However, the only Playwright additions in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` are UI checks for download/copy/close, and the file explicitly contains `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup code tests`. There is no e2e coverage for logging in with a backup code or asserting single-use rejection on a second attempt, so the finding is accurate and specific to the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:48 — Disabling 2FA with a backup code (valid, incorrect, and missing-codes cases, plus clearing backupCodes at line 107) is not covered by any test; the disable e2e test only uses TOTP.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new logic to the disable 2FA API to accept and validate `req.body.backupCode` (including MissingBackupCodes/IncorrectBackupCode branches) and clears `backupCodes` on disable (`data: { backupCodes: null, ... }`). In the only shown e2e test update (`apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`), there’s even a TODO/FIXME about adding backup code tests, and the flow still fills TOTP and does not exercise disabling 2FA via backup code. No other tests in the diff cover these new disable-with-backup-code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:53 — This assertion always passes: it calls `expect(...).toBeTruthy()` on an un-awaited isChecked() Promise, and the diff only adds a FIXME at line 50 instead of fixing it. Since the new flow leaves the backup-codes dialog open, the first test never checks that 2FA was enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` the line `await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` passes a `Promise<boolean>` into `expect(...)` without awaiting `isChecked()`. A Promise object is truthy, so `toBeTruthy()` can pass regardless of the switch state. The diff even adds a `FIXME` comment noting this, but does not fix it. (The claim that the new flow leaves the backup-codes dialog open is not supported here because the test now clicks `backup-codes-close` before asserting the switch has `data-state="checked"`.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:117 — The download test only checks the filename, with a TODO where a content check should be; it never checks that the file holds the 10 generated codes in xxxxx-xxxxx format.

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts, the newly added backup codes download test only asserts download.suggestedFilename() === "cal-backup-codes.txt" and explicitly leaves "// TODO: check file content". Given the diff adds logic to generate and format backup codes (10 codes, formatted via formatBackupCode to "xxxxx-xxxxx") and to create a Blob/URL for download in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, the test currently doesn’t verify that the downloaded file actually contains the expected 10 formatted codes—i.e., coverage is incomplete for this new behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:122 — The copy test only waits for a success toast (UI feedback), with a TODO where a clipboard check should be, so copying the wrong content or nothing would still pass.

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts the new “copy” test does `await page.getByTestId("backup-codes-copy").click();` and then only waits for the success toast (`await page.getByTestId("toast-success").waitFor();`) with an explicit `// TODO: check clipboard content`. As written, the test would still pass if the clipboard write failed or copied incorrect content, so it’s a concrete, diff-grounded gap in the new test’s assertion strength rather than an app bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:108 — No test checks that the backup codes shown in the UI match the encrypted users.backupCodes column, or that setup.ts:61 generates 10 unique 10-character hex codes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds backup-code generation/storage in `setup.ts` (`Array.from(Array(10), () => crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex"))` and encrypts/stores it in `users.backupCodes`) and adds UI to display/copy/download those codes, but the Playwright test only verifies the download filename and toast (`login.2fa.e2e.ts` around the newly added section) and even leaves TODOs to check file/clipboard content. There is no test asserting the displayed codes correspond to what was generated/stored (encrypted `users.backupCodes`), nor any test asserting the 10 generated codes are unique/10-char hex.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:41 — No negative e2e test covers an incorrect backup code at login or at disable (incorrect_backup_code error shown, login blocked), even though the TOTP path has an equivalent wrong-code check.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new backup-code authentication/disable flows and error handling (e.g., NextAuth authorize checks `credentials.backupCode` and can throw `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes`; disable API checks `req.body.backupCode` and returns the same errors). The Playwright suite only adds positive/UX checks for displaying/downloading/copying backup codes after enabling 2FA and even includes a TODO to add backup code tests, but it does not include a negative login/disable test asserting an incorrect backup code blocks the action and shows the `incorrect_backup_code` message. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a direct functional defect.
